sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 182 of 2008

Smt. Lakka Devi And Others
 Versus
 Dilip Singh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ramesh Prasad Gupta - Advocate for the appellants
 Shri S.N.Gajendragadkar- Advocate for respondent no. 3
 Company.
 Order
Being dissatisfied by the amount of compensation awarded by learned Tribunal vide award, dated
6/10/2007, passed by learned Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena in Claim
Case No.11

1/2007, the claimants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, seeking enhancement of compensation.

By the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have been awarded a compensation of Rs.2,91,000/-
alongwith interest @ 7% per annum from the date of application for the death of one Rameshwar (husband of appellant no.1 and father of appellant no.2 to 9), who succumbed to the injuries sustained by him in road accident occurred on 7/4/2006.
2.
The date of accident, the negligence and the issue of liability is not in dispute in this appeal.

The age of deceased to be 50 years at the time NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 2 MA-182-2008 of accident and his income at the rate of Rs.3,000/- per month also could not be disputed by parties to the appeal.
The learned counsel for the appellants however, challenged the impugned award on the ground that the Tribunal has illegally applied the multiplier of 11 instead of 13.
The dependency has been also wrongly taken as 1/3rd instead of 1/5th as there are nine dependents.
He also submitted that the Tribunal has also failed to give compensation towards general and non-pecuniary heads.
He therefore, submits that the amount of compensation needs to be suitably enhanced.

In support of his submissions, he placed reliance over the decisions of Apex Court in the matter of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr . reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104 and National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award passed by the Tribunal and submitted that the Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation.
The impugned award does not warrant any interference by this Court in the instant appeal.

4. Considered the arguments of both the sides and perused the record.
5.
There is no dispute with regard to the finding in respect of income of the deceased arrived at by the Tribunal at Rs.3,000/- per month.

However, in view of the judgment of Apex Court in the matter of Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to the compensation towards future prospects at the rate of 25%, looking to the age of the deceased as 50 years.

Since there are nine dependents, the dependency would also come to 1/5th NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 3 MA-182-2008 instead of 1/3rd.
The multiplier of 13 is applicable instead of 11 as applied by Tribunal.
Further, the appellants are also entitled to amount towards consortium @ 40,000/- each.
The appellants are also entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.

6. Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs.8,73,000/-, considering the annual income of deceased Rs.3,000/- per month and Rs.36,000/- per annum from which 1/5th is required to be deducted towards personal expenditure and after deducting the same, remaining amount comes to

Rs.
28,800/- to which 25% is required to be added towards future prospects and

after adding the same,
the amount comes to Rs.36,000/-, multiplier of 13 would be applicable and after applying the same,
total loss of dependency comes to Rs.36,000 x 13 = 4,68,000/-.
Adding, Rs.40,000/- for each 9 dependents under the head loss of consortium, Rs.3,60,000/- required to be added.
Thus, the total comes to Rs.8,28,000/-.

Further, adding Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses, the total amount of compensation comes to Rs.8,58,000/-.
The actual expenses of Rs.15,000/- towards medical expenses is also to be added.
The total amount of compensation then comes to Rs.8,73,000/-.

7. The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs.2,91,000/-, therefore, the appellants shall be entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.8,73,000 - 2,91,000 = Rs.5,82,000/-
(Rs. Five Lacs Eighty Two Thousands only).
The enhanced amount of compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of application till its actual payment.

The enhanced amount of compensation shall be payable to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 4 MA-182-2008 appellants by the Insurance Company within a period of 2 months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
8. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part with the aforesaid directions.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE JPS/-
